segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The lych gate stands at the top of the church path, and anybody crossing the green can see who is standing under it. Judith had chosen the spot on purpose. She had her list in her hand, folded, though she had no use for it now.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: I have written out what happened. The hour we set off, the place the wheel went, Nye's name and the hurdles, and the hour we came in. I mean to say it at the library counter tomorrow with Mrs Hale standing there, and then to Mrs Yardley, and then to Sarah Copp's mother, who is the one that put the crying in.

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: They will not believe it.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: Some of them will. And the rest will have to say it to my face or not at all, and I would rather be laughed at in front of me than pitied behind me. I know what it will cost. I shall stand in a shop and explain a cracked spoke to fools, and be very civil about it, and go home and be sick with temper for two days. I have done it before.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He had been holding his hat. He put it on the gate post, which was the nearest thing to putting down a shield that a curate can manage.

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: I do not want it corrected.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: I beg your pardon?

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: I would rather it were made true. There is no dinner arranged round this, and nobody has told me what neckcloth to wear, and Mrs Pike does not know I am standing here. I am asking whether you would have me. Eighty a year, and no expectations, and two rooms over Mrs Copp's that look at a wall.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Judith did not answer at once. She had been asked nothing at all in seven-and-twenty years, and she had promised herself walking up the hill that she would not be grateful.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: Answer me one thing first, and answer it exactly. Do you ask because you want me, or because it would tidy the parish up? Because a man may be very kind and still be only mending a wheel.

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: In November you told me it was Chronicles.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: That is not an answer.

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: It is the whole of it. I have thought about that morning perhaps three hundred times since. I told myself I was nursing an injury. A man does not go over the same half minute for eight months out of injury, Miss Vane, he does it because he cannot leave off looking at the person in it. And I have thought of that list on the green nearly as often, and every time I have wanted to go back and take it, and read the six, and come and tell you what I thought of them. That is not tidiness. Tidiness would have been Miss Marchmont, and I could not think of a thing to say to her but the weather.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Judith laughed. It got away from her entirely, and she put the folded paper up against her mouth, and it did not help.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: You said the rain was seasonable.

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: I did.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: Four days out of seven.

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: Judith.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: Yes. Yes, I will have you, and you may stop turning your hat about, because it is on the gate post.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It was a little after five, and the sun was still well up over the mill. She took the folded paper and put it in her pocket unread by anybody, and he took his hat, and they came down the church path and out onto the green side by side, at a walking pace, in the full light of a Monday afternoon.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The library window was bright above the draper's, and there was somebody in it.

segments.speaker: Miss Judith Vane
segments.text: Do not hurry.

segments.speaker: Mr Silas Rowe
segments.text: I had not the least intention of it.
